svg.title: A point, an arrow, and an angle
svg.desc: A whiteboard sketch showing the vector (3,4) drawn both as a red dot and as a blue arrow from the origin with its 3-4-5 right triangle and the norm worked out as five; two arrows u and v with the angle between them marked and the dot product formula written out with cosine theta circled; three document vectors showing that a short and a long document about cats point the same way while a tax-law document is ninety degrees away, with the Euclidean distance between the two cat documents struck through in red; a unit circle with the same arrows normalised onto it; and two histograms of pairwise distances that are wide at two dimensions and collapse to a thin spike at a thousand.
svg.text: A point, an arrow, and an angle
a vector is a POINT and an ARROW
the two cat docs are FAR apart (Euclidean)
every vector pulled onto the unit circle:
now cosine IS a plain dot product -
one BLAS call, not a Python loop.
do not normalise TWICE. Half the retrieval
bugs in week 27 are a vector normalised at
write time and again at read time.
max/min distance: 2838x at d=2, 1.10x at d=1000
everything is the same distance from everything
...so how do you search a million of
